name: GPTQ (one-shot approximate second-order PTQ)
quality_delta: From the GPTQ paper: OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B quantized to 3-4 bits in ~4 GPU hours with 'minimal increase in perplexity'; the bespoke execution kernels give ~3.25x on A100 and 4.5x on A6000 (quant-gptq-paper). The paper's Figure 1 is a ppl-vs-RTN comparison against the FP16 baseline and is a figure, not tabulated numbers, so no single delta value is recorded here.
notes: Weight-only, 16-bit compute. GPTQ's contribution is the rounding criterion (approximate inverse Hessian from calibration), not a new number format - a GPTQ file is INT4/INT3 with per-group scales, the same layout AWQ produces, which is why the two share every serving kernel. Group size 128 is the conventional default; 32/64/1024 are legal and change both quality and kernel eligibility, which is a frequent source of 'GPTQ is slow' reports. EXL2 is a GPTQ derivative with per-tensor variable bitrate and should be read alongside this record. exllamav2's own throughput table (3090 Ti / 4090) lists GPTQ at grpsz 128 at 181 and 205 tok/s for Llama-7B (quant-exl2-readme) - a third-party number for the runtime, not a quality delta.
